key_insight: Equipping training-free VLN agents with a lightweight metacognitive layer that monitors progress, diagnoses failure modes (e.g., oscillation, redundancy), and adapts exploration strategy significantly reduces wandering and improves navigation efficiency.
problem_solved: Existing foundation-model powered VLN agents use greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, causing local oscillation and redundant revisits because they lack self-monitoring and adaptive decision-making.
method: Add a metacognitive module that continuously evaluates exploration progress and detects failure patterns (stuck, oscillation, low information gain) using promptable foundation models and simple heuristics.
Use diagnosis signals to adapt frontier scoring, re-prioritize targets, and update an active spatial memory (marking visited/low-value regions) so the agent avoids revisits and oscillatory loops.
Integrate the metacognitive loop with existing training-free controllers/planners for on-the-fly re-planning—no extra end-to-end training required.
impact: Provides a practical, training-free way to make VLN agents more efficient and robust, reducing wasted steps and improving real-world deployability of embodied agents. Practitioners can integrate metacognitive checks to boost performance without costly retraining.
